title: Orchestrated evacuation and shadow-tiling for variant rollout
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Add a lightweight orchestration layer that coordinates progressive shadowing, emergency evacuation (spillover) from overloaded tiers/regions, and per-variant compatibility shims during canary/A-B rollouts. This ticket focuses on the routing policy and state machine used by the controller — not the UI. The controller must make deterministic, auditable decisions about when to divert shadow traffic, when to activate evacuation lanes (e.g., throttle or move traffic from dedicated -> hosted), and how to attach per-variant compatibility transforms so consumers see consistent behavior across tier/region transitions.
background_and_rationale: We frequently see partial regressions during canaries that only appear under cross-region load or when capacity tiers are saturated. Current fallbacks are ad-hoc per-service and hard to reason about. A dedicated orchestrator will centralize decisions (evacuation, spillover, shadow-tiling) and make rollouts more robust across Dedicated/Hosted/Private deployments while preserving SLOs and minimizing customer-visible variance.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic state machine exists for routing decisions (states: NORMAL, PROBING, SHADOW_ONLY, EVACUATION, COMPACT) and is covered by unit tests
Controller can atomically flip a traffic lane to shadow-only mode for a tenant or model variant without dropping live traffic
Evacuation policy supports tiered targets: hosted -> dedicated -> private (configurable per-customer) and logs each decision with trace IDs
Per-variant transform hooks (compatibility shims) can be applied on the outbound routing path to normalize responses when a variant switch occurs
End-to-end integration test demonstrating spillover from a saturated eu-west region to us-east with transparent routing and no request loss

Observability: dashboard with evacuation events, shadow-tiling ratios, compatibility-shim activations, and a rollback metric that triggers alerting when >5% of requests fail post-rollout for 5 minutes
design_decisions: Use a central controller service (stateless instances) backed by a strongly-consistent control plane (current ZK/consul cluster) to avoid race conditions during flips
Traffic rules expressed as layered policies: hard constraints (capacity/region), soft preferences (latency/cost), and safety overrides (SLO breaches)
Shadow-tiling will use deterministic hashing to ensure per-tenant sticky shadow buckets so we can attribute regressions reliably
Compatibility shims implemented as lightweight, versioned transforms registered per model variant using runtime hooks (no model binary changes)
Evacuation uses a graceful drain window with token-based admission to avoid sudden cold-start spikes in target capacity
implementation_notes: Controller API endpoints: POST /orchestrator/v1/flip, GET /orchestrator/v1/status, POST /orchestrator/v1/probe
State transitions are recorded as events in event-sink (kafka topic ‘orchestrator.events’) with correlation_id for tracing
Introduce a new routing key in the runtime: 'evacuation_priority' (int) and 'shadow_bucket' (uint32 hash)
Add hooks in the routing cache layer to apply 'compatibility_shim_id' when routing to an older/newer variant
Fail-open semantics: if control plane unreachable, continue on last known policy for up to 5 minutes, then escalate
testing_plan: Unit tests for state machine transitions covering abnormal paths (control plane loss, inconsistent metrics)
Integration test using the load harness to simulate region saturation and verify spillover without increased error rate
Chaos test: kill a subset of controller instances during an in-progress evacuation and assert deterministic outcome
Regression test that runs a sample of existing canary playbooks to ensure no existing rollback behavior is broken
Synthetic traffic job that exercises compatibility shims across 3 variants and validates output normalization
rollout_plan: Stage 1 (internal): Deploy controller to staging only, run synthetic suite, validate metrics
Stage 2 (opt-in tenants): Enable shadow-tiling for a small set of power users (5 tenants) and monitor for 48 hours
Stage 3 (regional pilot): Enable evacuation policies in us-east and eu-west for non-critical namespaces, simulate saturation
Stage 4 (global): Flip on controller with read-only mode for 1 week, then allow active flips with automated rollbacks enabled
Rollback strategy: automated rollback when post-rollout user-facing error-rate delta > 2x baseline for 10 minutes, with manual override via OnCall
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboards: Orchestrator > Events, Shadow-tiling > Ratio by tenant, Evacuation > Active windows and endpoints
Alerts: 'evacuation-failure' when target capacity rejects >1% of evacuated tokens for 5m
SLO-based alert: 'post-rollout-regression' when user-visible error rate increases 2x within rollout window
Audit log retention: all flips written to audit-store for 90 days with tenant, variant, and correlation_id
Tracing: attach controller correlation_id to per-request trace for end-to-end debugging
